model_annotation: The plot is a line chart illustrating the relationship between co-occurrence numbers and accuracy (ACC) percentages for different models such as Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME. The x-axis represents the quantity of co-occurrences, plotted on a logarithmic scale with values ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The y-axis shows the accuracy percentage, marked at intervals of 5, spanning from 40% to 65%. Each model is represented by a line with unique markers and colors for distinction. The Base model exhibits a static ACC across the co-occurrence numbers, remaining constant near the lower end of the ACC range. The MEND model shows a slight increase in ACC with rising co-occurrence numbers. FT’s line trends upwards significantly as its erratic path crosses through ACC values from 40% to 60%. MEMIT's ACC exhibits a steady increase reaching closer to 55% at the highest co-occurrence. IKE shows a marked increase in accuracy, starting above the Base model and a bit upwards of MEMIT. The ROME model demonstrates the highest ACC, starting just below the MID point at 50% and showing a significant climb up along the co-occurrence numbers to approximately 65%.
